questions.text:
What is the time complexity of Bellman-Ford single-source shortest path algorithm on a complete
graph of n vertices?
questions.solution:
Bellman-Ford takes [latex]\Theta(VE)[/latex]. A complete graph has [latex]E=\Theta(n^2)[/latex].

[latex]n\times n^2=\Theta(n^3)[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\Theta(n^3)[/latex]

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are TRUE?
1. The problem of determining whether there exists a cycle in an undirected graph is in P.
2. The problem of determining whether there exists a cycle in an undirected graph is in NP.
3. If a problem A is NP-Complete, there exists a non-deterministic polynomial time algorithm to solve A.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- 1: cycle detection by DFS is polynomial [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] in P
- 2: P [latex]\subseteq[/latex] NP [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] also in NP
- 3: NP-complete problems are in NP, so they have a non-deterministic polynomial algorithm

Answer: 1, 2 and 3

questions.text:
Which one of the following is the tightest upper bound that represents the number of swaps
required to sort n numbers using selection sort?
questions.solution:
Selection sort does at most one swap per pass, so at most n [latex]-[/latex] 1 swaps.

Answer: O(n)

questions.text: Consider the directed graph shown in the figure below. There are multiple shortest paths between vertices S and T. Which one will be reported by Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm? Assume that, in any iteration, the shortest path to a vertex v is updated only when a strictly shorter path to v is discovered
questions.solution:
Dijkstra from S: B = 3, A = 4, D = 7 (via S).
- Pop B: D via B = 7, not strictly shorter, so D keeps parent S.
- Pop A: C = 5. Pop C: E = 6 (D via C = 8, no change).
- Pop E: T = 10 (via E), G = 8.
- Pop D: T via D = 10, not strictly shorter, so T keeps parent E.

Path: S [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] A [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] C [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] E [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T

Answer: SACET

questions.text:
A list of n strings, each of length n, is sorted into lexicographic order using the merge-sort
algorithm. The worst case running time of this computation is
questions.solution:
Merge sort makes [latex]O(n\log n)[/latex] comparisons. Each comparison of two n-length strings can take O(n).

Total = [latex]O(n^2\log n)[/latex]

Answer: [latex]O(n^2\log n)[/latex]
